candidates.name: El Sadat–El Fayoum (Dahshour) Gas Pipeline

evidence.note: GASCO Environmental Impact Assessment for the El Sadat–El Fayoum gas pipeline: 76 km length, 32-inch diameter, runs south from El Sadat off-take room parallel to the SUMED and El Ameriya–Dashour lines through 6th of October City, terminating at Dahshour compression station; purpose to increase gas delivered to Upper Egypt and Cairo.

EIB EGAS Gas Grid Reinforcement project: five large-diameter pipelines totaling ~835 km reinforcing the eastern and southern national high-pressure transmission system; segments include Elnubaria–Elsadat, Elsadat–Elfayoum, and Gerga–Aswan.

candidates.why_maybe_new: No roster row runs El Sadat -> Dahshour/El Fayoum. P3928 (Nubaria–Sadat) is the upstream segment and P3930 (New Administrative Capital–Dahshur) reaches Dahshour from a different origin; this 76 km 32-inch trunk between El Sadat and Dahshour compression station appears uncaptured.

candidates.name: Taba–Sharm El-Sheikh Gas Pipeline

evidence.note: OGJ: GASCO began building the Taba/Sharm El-Sheikh line in 2006; 220 km of 20-inch pipe, up to 6 MMcfd, went online early 2007 at ~511 million EGP, serving Taba, Nuweiba, Dahab and Sharm El-Sheikh (cities, hotels, tourist villages, power stations) in South Sinai.

candidates.why_maybe_new: Roster has P0436 (Arish–Taba) and P7482 (Taba–Aqaba sea line) at the Taba node but no line running south down the Sinai east coast to Sharm El-Sheikh; this 220 km 20-inch South Sinai transmission trunk has no roster match.

candidates.name: Shukeir–Hurghada Gas Pipeline

evidence.note: OGJ: GASCO completed the Shukeir–Hurghada line in 2006; 127 km of 24-inch pipe, up to 7 MMcfd, ~336 million EGP, feeding cities and power stations of the Red Sea Governorate along the coast.

candidates.why_maybe_new: Roster has P6034 (Hurghada–Safaga, 38.5 km, 24-inch) continuing south of Hurghada but no line feeding Hurghada from Shukeir on the Gulf of Suez; this 127 km 24-inch Red Sea coast transmission trunk appears uncaptured (P6034 may be its downstream continuation).
